title: Geo-legal matrix + pinning decision log
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures the canonical geo-legal decision matrix we use to decide when customer data must be pinned to a region (or country), how to score legal risk, what enforcement controls are required, and the operational flow for exceptions, migrations, and incidents. It is intended for engineers implementing pinning controls, product managers documenting customer commitments, and legal/compliance reviewers.

Scope and definitions:
- Pinning: making an individual customer's inference requests and persistent artifacts (models, KV caches, logs, audit entries) only routable to and stored within specified geographic boundaries.
- Residency-required: legal/regulatory mandate (statute or regulator guidance) that requires non-transferrable local storage/processing.
- Residency-preferred: strong contractual or sector guidance where customers expect local processing but an exception may be negotiated.
- Cross-border flow: any invocation or background job that would move identifiable customer data outside the pinned boundary.

Decision matrix (summary):
Columns: Region | Triggering law / operator | Minimum enforcement level | Recommended infra controls | Risk score (1-10)
- EU (GDPR + member state regs) | If customer is an EU entity or processes sensitive EU personal data | Level: Contractual pin + technical routing | Controls: VPC subnet affinity, region pin flag, egress blocklists, per-tenant KV partitioning, audit logs | 7
- UK | UK GDPR / Data Protection Act | Level: Contractual pin + optional hard enforcement for regulated sectors | Controls: Similar to EU, with optional dedicated storage zone | 6
- India | Localisation laws (finance/telecom draft guidance) | Level: Preferred for certain regulated verticals; escalate if regulator guidance finalizes | Controls: Soft pin (policy + routing preference), monitoring for cross-border flows | 6
- Brazil (LGPD) | LGPD + sector guidance | Level: Contractual pin recommended for fin/health | Controls: region routing, retention policies, legal review for transfers | 5
- APAC financial hubs (e.g., Singapore, Hong Kong) | Sector-specific guidance | Level: Sector-driven; usually contractual + operational | Controls: per-tenant region configuration, SLA notes | 5
- Sovereign-only scenarios (air-gapped / government) | Explicit customer requirement | Level: Hard pin + dedicated private deployment | Controls: On-prem or private VPC deployment, KMS enforced locally, no cross-border backups | 10

Risk scoring guidance (how to pick a number):
- Base 1-3: voluntary localisation or weak guidance; easy to satisfy via contractual commitments and controls.
- Base 4-6: established data protection frameworks where regulators have enforcement history.
- Base 7-10: explicit lawful requirement or government customer; requires technical enforcement and enterprise legal sign-off.
Adjust up for: regulated vertical (finance, healthcare), presence of sensitive personal data, sector audits.

Enforcement levels (detailed):
- Policy-only (soft): Documented contract clause + routing preference. Helpful for sales/prod but not enforced by infra. Use when risk score <=4.
- Tech-preventive: Requests are preferred to pinned region, but system can fallback to other regions under capacity or outage. Add tagging/logging + periodic audit. Use for risk 5-7 unless legal requires hard enforcement.
- Hard-enforced (no egress): Network and runtime controls that prevent serving or storing data outside the pinned region. Requires private/dedicated deployments or strict cloud region controls. Use for risk >=8 or explicit legal mandate.

Operational controls (implementation checklist):
- Tenant-level metadata: add fields pin_regions (list), pin_mode (policy|prefer|enforce).
- Routing layer: evaluate request region affinity before routing. If pin_mode=enforce and destination incompatible, return 403 + error code PINNED_REGION_MISMATCH.
- Storage layer: enforce bucket/DB partition per region + ensure backups follow same residency.
- KV cache: segregate per-tenant caches; do not replicate across regions for enforce mode.
- Telemetry: emit residency-tagged traces, per-request residency decision reason, and counters for cross-boundary fallbacks.
- Infra guardrails: egress firewall policies, IAM policies preventing accidental snapshots to global buckets, and CI checks for infra changes that may widen data movement.

Exception process (short form):
1) Requestor (sales, solutions) raises a Residency Exception (RE) ticket with business justification, expected duration, data types, and risk mitigation plan.
2) Compliance/legal triage: issue preliminary risk rating and required controls.
3) Engineering impact assessment: feasibility, cost, time estimate to meet requested controls.
4) Decision: Approve with mitigation, Approve temporary (timeboxed), or Deny. Record decision in the decision log and notify customer.
SLA: Compliance team responds in 3 business days, engineering impact assessment in 7 business days.

Decision log example entries (format):
- ID: RE-2024-211 | Customer: FinUp Ltd | Region request: EU | Data types: inference + logs | Requested: enforce | Outcome: Approve-temporary (90d) with migration plan | Notes: Use dedicated EU VPC; customer to sign addendum.
- ID: RE-2024-233 | Customer: MedCo | Region request: Sovereign | Data types: PHI | Outcome: Approve -> Private on-prem deployment | Notes: Contract + SOC review required.

Migration playbook (for customers moving from multi-region to pinned region):
- Pre-migration steps: obtain addendum signed; validate target region capacity; schedule maintenance window; copy non-restricted artifacts to target region with integrity checks.
- Cutover: freeze writes to global store for TTL window, switch routing to new tenant-region, rotate keys, monitor for errors and latency regressions.
- Post-migration: run audit to ensure no artifacts remain in external regions; update billing & telemetry; notify customer and CS.
- Rollback: maintain an immediate rollback plan for first 48 hours and warm routes to global fallback in case of perf/regression issues.

Monitoring and audit signals to maintain:
- Per-tenant egress attempts count (should be zero in enforce mode).
- Cross-region cache hits/misses for pinned tenants.
- Last-seen storage locations for persistent artifacts.
- Weekly residency compliance report emitted to Compliance slack channel and stored in the contract folder.

On-call playbook for residency incidents:
- Trigger: detection of cross-border egress attempt for enforce-mode tenant OR storage found outside pinned region.
- Triage steps: 1) Page oncall-residency, 2) Collect request traces and affected tenant ids, 3) Quarantine offending path (block egress), 4) Notify legal & customer success, 5) Run containment migration if accidental.
- Post-incident: create RCA, remediate infra gap, update decision log and playbook.

Policy templates and artifacts to maintain (locations):
- Contract clause template: CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM/Residency-Clauses
- Engineering spec: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/pinning
- Audit checklist: S3/Azure/GSuite backup verification script (internal repo link in linked_artifacts).

Open questions / items for follow-up:
- Final legal guidance on recent APAC finance draft — impact on scoring and whether we should shift India to hard-enforce for some verticals. Owner: Lina Chen.
- Automation: should the Compliance sign-off step be a light-weight digital approval in the Console? UX spike to be scoped. Owner: Marco Ruiz.
- Cost model: estimate monthly incremental cost for hard-enforced EU pin at scale. Owner: Finance (cc Samir).

Appendix: minimal Jira template to raise a residency exception (copy-paste):
Title: Residency Exception Request — <customer> — <region>
Description:
- Customer name:
- Customer legal entity / jurisdiction:
- Data types in scope:
- Requested residency behavior (policy|prefer|enforce):
- Business justification:
- Expected duration (if temporary):
- Suggested mitigations / compensations:
- Attach signed addendum (if available):

Footer: last updated 2025-02-14 by Asha Patel. Keep this doc as the single source for scoring rules and operational steps; update entries in the decision log as exceptions are approved or denied.
